tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool classifies low-complexity intervals by their repeat unit. The intervals can come from a masker such as dustmasker, tantan or windowmasker. The BED name column then shows what each interval contains, not the name of the masker.
For each interval, the tool tries periods 1 to 6 and keeps the shortest period whose consensus matches at least 85% of the bases. If no period does this, it keeps the period with the best match. Each output row has these columns:
- **name**: the repeat-unit signature. Period 1 gives ``polyA``, ``polyT`` and so on. Periods 2 to 6 give ``(AT)n``, ``(AAT)n`` and so on. If the purity is below 60%, the name is ``lc``. - **score**: the purity × 1000, from 0 to 1000. The purity is the fraction of bases that match the consensus. - **strand**: always ``.``.
-----
**Inputs**
- A FASTA file, plain or gzip-compressed. - A BED file of intervals on that FASTA. The tool accepts BED3 or more columns. It uses only the first three columns.
**Output**
A BED6 file, sorted by chromosome and start.
-----
**Notes**
- The tool converts the sequence to uppercase first. Soft-masked input thus gives the same result. - The tool splits each interval at runs of ``N`` and classifies each piece separately. An interval that contains only ``N`` gives no output row. - The tool does not detect repeat units longer than 6 bp. Such an interval usually gives ``lc``. - The tool stops with an error and writes no output if: - the BED names a sequence that is not in the FASTA, or - an interval is empty or lies outside its sequence. - The tool reads the FASTA one record at a time. Memory use thus stays low on large assemblies.
